title: The waterfall and V models: testing as a mirror of the requirement

videos.script: Requirements, then design, then code, then testing, then release. One phase after another, like water down a staircase. {{steps}} That is the waterfall. And the man usually credited with it called it risky, in the same paper. {{royce}} Testing comes last, so it is the first moment anything meets reality. And when the schedule slips, testing is the phase that gets squeezed. {{squeezed}} The V model keeps the sequence, and folds it in half. {{fold}} Every description on the way down has a test on the way up. Requirements, and acceptance testing. Design, and system testing. Architecture, and integration. Modules, and unit tests. {{pairs}} Its real gift is timing. Each test can be designed the day its description is written, and that is when ambiguities surface. {{timing}} Then we apply the four levels to the cinema's shop, and keep a matrix that links every requirement to its tests. {{matrix}} And we finish with where the sequence breaks. {{end}}
